# Connecting

Every workflow starts the same way: open a session to the pool's coordinator, accepting its certificate (hosts ship with a self-signed one) and logging in. If you connect to a pool member instead, login fails with `HOST_IS_SLAVE` naming the coordinator, and these helpers reconnect there, as XenCenter does.

[All workflows](README.md)

## C# (.NET)

```csharp
private static Session Connect(string url, string user, string password)
{
    try
    {
        return Login(url, user, password);
    }
    catch (Failure f) when (f.ErrorDescription[0] == "HOST_IS_SLAVE")
    {
        // A pool member names the coordinator's address; reconnect there (assuming the coordinator
        // is up), exactly as XenCenter does when you add a member server.
        return Login($"https://{f.ErrorDescription[1]}", user, password);
    }
}

private static Session Login(string url, string user, string password)
{
    var session = new Session(url);
    // Accept the host's self-signed certificate.
    session.JsonRpcClient.ServerCertificateValidationCallback = (req, cert, chain, errors) => true;
    session.login_with_password(user, password, "1.0", "sdk-examples");
    return session;
}

// Look up a template VM by its exact name (rather than picking an arbitrary one).
private static string TemplateByName(Session session, string name) =>
    VM.get_all_records(session).First(kv => kv.Value.is_a_template && kv.Value.name_label == name)
        .Key.opaque_ref;

// Look up a guest VM (not a template, control domain or snapshot) by its exact name.
private static string VmByName(Session session, string name) =>
    VM.get_all_records(session).First(kv => !kv.Value.is_a_template && !kv.Value.is_control_domain
        && !kv.Value.is_a_snapshot && kv.Value.name_label == name).Key.opaque_ref;

// Look up an SR by its exact name (optionally requiring it to be shared).
private static string SrByName(Session session, string name, bool shared = false) =>
    SR.get_all_records(session).First(kv => kv.Value.name_label == name && (!shared || kv.Value.shared))
        .Key.opaque_ref;

/// <summary>
/// Detach an SR from every host, then forget it: XenCenter's Detach followed by Forget. SR.forget
/// refuses an SR that is still attached (SR_HAS_PBD), so unplug its PBDs first. Forgetting drops the
/// pool's record of the SR but leaves the data on the storage itself.
/// </summary>
private static void DetachAndForgetSr(Session session, string sr)
{
    foreach (var pbd in SR.get_PBDs(session, sr))
        if (PBD.get_currently_attached(session, pbd.opaque_ref))
            PBD.unplug(session, pbd.opaque_ref);
    SR.forget(session, sr);
}

/// <summary>
/// VM.provision, after filling in the SR for every disk the template describes. A template's
/// other_config["disks"] carries each disk's SR as sr="" (empty); a real host takes that literally and
/// VM.provision fails with UUID_INVALID, so the caller has to rewrite it to the pool's default SR
/// first — exactly what `xe vm-install` does before calling VM.provision itself.
/// </summary>
private static void Provision(Session session, string vm)
{
    if (VM.get_other_config(session, vm).TryGetValue("disks", out var disksXml))
    {
        var defaultSr = Pool.get_default_SR(session, Pool.get_all(session).First().opaque_ref).opaque_ref;
        var doc = XDocument.Parse(disksXml);
        foreach (var disk in doc.Root!.Elements("disk"))
            disk.SetAttributeValue("sr", SR.get_uuid(session, defaultSr));

        VM.remove_from_other_config(session, vm, "disks");
        VM.add_to_other_config(session, vm, "disks", doc.ToString(SaveOptions.DisableFormatting));
    }
    VM.provision(session, vm);
}

/// <summary>The first (from the end) Failure detail that looks like an XML fragment, or null.</summary>
private static string XmlFromFailure(Failure f) =>
    f.ErrorDescription.AsEnumerable().Reverse()
        .FirstOrDefault(d => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(d) && d.TrimStart().StartsWith("<"));

/// <summary>
/// Return the XML a backend sends back on its deliberately-failing discovery probe. The New SR
/// wizard (and XenRT) discover iSCSI/HBA LUNs by asking with an incomplete device-config on purpose:
/// the backend can't create anything from it yet, so it fails with an SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_&lt;n&gt;
/// error whose params carry an XML fragment describing what it found. Never probe by attempting
/// SR.create instead: on real storage a create that unexpectedly succeeds formats the LUN.
/// </summary>
private static string ProbeForFailure(Session session, string host,
    Dictionary<string, string> deviceConfig, string smType)
{
    try
    {
        SR.probe(session, host, deviceConfig, smType, new Dictionary<string, string>());
    }
    catch (Failure f)
    {
        var xml = XmlFromFailure(f);
        if (xml != null) return xml;
        throw;
    }
    throw new Exception($"SR.probe for {smType} succeeded without asking for more information; " +
                        "check the target address");
}

// Pick the IQN from an iSCSI discovery probe: the caller's, if named (it must be one the target
// offers), else the first. An array usually offers many targets - one per LUN, often belonging to
// different users - so on shared storage always name yours: SR.create formats the LUN behind it.
private static string ChooseTargetIqn(XDocument iqnXml, string target, string targetIqn)
{
    var offered = iqnXml.Descendants("TargetIQN").Select(e => e.Value).ToList();
    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(targetIqn) && !offered.Contains(targetIqn))
        throw new Exception($"target {target} does not offer IQN {targetIqn}");
    return string.IsNullOrEmpty(targetIqn) ? offered.First() : targetIqn;
}

/// <summary>
/// A throwaway self-signed certificate and private key (PEM), the way XenRT provisions one for its
/// own certificate tests. .NET's own X509 API builds one directly - no external tool needed.
/// </summary>
private static (string CertPem, string KeyPem) SelfSignedCertPem()
{
    using var rsa = RSA.Create(2048);
    var request = new System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.CertificateRequest(
        "CN=sdk-example", rsa, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, RSASignaturePadding.Pkcs1);
    using var cert = request.CreateSelfSigned(
        DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(-1), DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(365));
    return (cert.ExportCertificatePem(), rsa.ExportRSAPrivateKeyPem());
}

/// <summary>
/// Wait out a pool-wide xapi restart (Pool.designate_new_master) and reconnect.
///
/// designate_new_master returns BEFORE the change: for a while the old coordinator still answers,
/// and still says it is the coordinator, until xapi restarts across the pool. So reconnecting is not
/// enough - keep reconnecting until the pool names the new coordinator (by uuid; Connect follows
/// HOST_IS_SLAVE to wherever the coordinator now is). XenRT's own helper likewise waits minutes
/// before trusting the pool again.
/// </summary>
private static Session ReconnectAfterMasterChange(string url, string user, string password,
    string newMasterUuid, int timeoutSeconds = 600, int intervalSeconds = 5)
{
    var deadline = DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(timeoutSeconds);
    object lastError = null;
    while (DateTime.UtcNow < deadline)
    {
        try
        {
            var session = Connect(url, user, password);
            var master = Pool.get_master(session, Pool.get_all(session)[0].opaque_ref).opaque_ref;
            // The new coordinator answers before the pool has settled - calls made too soon fail
            // (HANDLE_INVALID on the operation's own task) - so also wait for every host to be back,
            // live and enabled.
            if (Host.get_uuid(session, master) == newMasterUuid && Host.get_all_records(session).Values.All(
                    r => r.enabled && Host_metrics.get_live(session, r.metrics.opaque_ref)))
                return session;
            session.logout();
            lastError = "the pool has not settled under the new coordinator";
        }
        catch (Exception e)
        {
            lastError = e;
        }
        System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(intervalSeconds * 1000);
    }
    throw new Exception($"the pool did not come back after the master change: {lastError}");
}

/// <summary>
/// Poll host_metrics.live until it matches, rather than issuing the next power command immediately -
/// real out-of-band power control has no retry of its own, so a tool that doesn't wait can issue a
/// second command while the first is still in flight.
/// </summary>
private static void WaitForHostLive(Session session, string host, bool want,
    int timeoutSeconds = 60, int intervalSeconds = 2)
{
    var deadline = DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(timeoutSeconds);
    while (HostLive(session, host) != want)
    {
        if (DateTime.UtcNow > deadline) throw new Exception($"host did not reach live={want} in time");
        System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(intervalSeconds * 1000);
    }
}

/// <summary>
/// Wait for a host to come back from a reboot (key "boot_time") or toolstack restart
/// ("agent_start_time"): until that other_config entry differs from <paramref name="before"/> and the
/// host is live. Reconnects every time round, because the host restarting may be the coordinator this
/// session talks to; returns the new session.
/// </summary>
private static Session WaitForRestart(string url, string user, string password, string hostUuid,
    string key, string before, int timeoutSeconds = 1800, int intervalSeconds = 10)
{
    var deadline = DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(timeoutSeconds);
    while (true)
    {
        try
        {
            var session = Connect(url, user, password);
            var host = Host.get_by_uuid(session, hostUuid).opaque_ref;
            var otherConfig = Host.get_other_config(session, host);
            var value = otherConfig.TryGetValue(key, out var v) ? v : null;
            if (value != before && HostLive(session, host))
                return session;
            session.logout();
        }
        catch (Exception)
        {
            // down, or xapi still starting
        }
        if (DateTime.UtcNow > deadline) throw new Exception($"host {hostUuid} did not come back in time");
        System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(intervalSeconds * 1000);
    }
}

/// <summary>
/// Re-enable a host that has just come back. It reports itself live before xapi on it has finished
/// starting, and until then Host.enable fails HOST_STILL_BOOTING - so retry that.
/// </summary>
private static void EnableWhenBooted(Session session, string host, int timeoutSeconds = 600,
    int intervalSeconds = 10)
{
    var deadline = DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(timeoutSeconds);
    while (true)
    {
        try
        {
            Host.enable(session, host);
            return;
        }
        catch (Failure e)
        {
            if (e.ErrorDescription[0] != "HOST_STILL_BOOTING" || DateTime.UtcNow > deadline) throw;
            System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(intervalSeconds * 1000);
        }
    }
}

/// <summary>
/// Build the URL for a given host's own address, keeping the scheme and port the caller originally
/// connected with (a host's management address carries no port of its own).
/// </summary>
private static string HostUrl(string url, string address)
{
    var uri = new Uri(url);
    var port = uri.IsDefaultPort ? "" : $":{uri.Port}";
    return $"{uri.Scheme}://{address}{port}";
}

/// <summary>
/// Relocate every one of a (not-yet-started) VM's disks onto the given SR, the same VDI.pool_migrate
/// storage-migrate already demonstrates.
/// </summary>
private static void MoveDisksToSr(Session session, string vm, string srRef)
{
    foreach (var vdi in DiskVdis(session, vm))
        if (VDI.get_SR(session, vdi).opaque_ref != srRef)
            AwaitTask(session, VDI.async_pool_migrate(session, vdi, srRef, new Dictionary<string, string>()));
}

/// <summary>
/// Wait for an async_* task to finish, return its result and destroy it. A call that copies a disk
/// runs for many minutes, and an HTTP request held open that long tends to be dropped by the network
/// (SocketException 10060) however long the client is willing to wait, so long operations start the
/// async_ twin, which returns a Task at once, and poll that instead.
/// </summary>
private static string AwaitTask(Session session, XenRef<Task> task)
{
    try
    {
        while (Task.get_status(session, task) == task_status_type.pending)
            System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(1000);
        if (Task.get_status(session, task) != task_status_type.success)
            throw new Failure(Task.get_error_info(session, task));
        return Task.get_result(session, task).Replace("<value>", "").Replace("</value>", "").Trim();
    }
    finally
    {
        Task.destroy(session, task);
    }
}

/// <summary>
/// A throwaway VM with a working guest OS: a copy of an existing VM that has one. Suspend,
/// checkpoint, live migration and clean shutdown all need the guest's cooperation: on a running VM
/// with no PV drivers xapi refuses them up front with VM_LACKS_FEATURE (a VM freshly cloned from a
/// template has no OS at all). So copy a VM that does have an OS and PV drivers, without disturbing
/// it: snapshot it (fine while it runs), clone the snapshot - a clone of a snapshot is a template -
/// and provision that into an ordinary VM. The snapshot is only needed for the clone, so it goes
/// again straight away.
/// </summary>
private static string CopyOfGuest(Session session, string sourceVmName, string newVmName)
{
    var source = VmByName(session, sourceVmName);
    var snapshot = VM.snapshot(session, source, newVmName + "-source").opaque_ref;
    var vm = VM.clone(session, snapshot, newVmName).opaque_ref;
    Provision(session, vm);
    DestroyVmAndDisks(session, snapshot);
    return vm;
}

/// <summary>
/// Wait, after VM.start, until the guest's PV drivers have reported in. xapi only offers the
/// guest-dependent operations once the guest says it can do them, and allowed_operations is where
/// it says so: wait for clean_shutdown to appear there (the same check that refuses it with
/// VM_LACKS_FEATURE beforehand). A booting OS takes a while.
/// </summary>
private static void WaitForGuestAgent(Session session, string vm, int timeoutSeconds = 300,
    int intervalSeconds = 2)
{
    // clean_shutdown in allowed_operations says the guest can shut down; a Linux kernel offers that early
    // in boot, before the agent runs (hot-plug needs the agent, and suspend needs its emulated disk
    // unplugged), so wait for the guest metrics to report the PV drivers too.
    bool Ready()
    {
        if (!VM.get_allowed_operations(session, vm).Contains(vm_operations.clean_shutdown)) return false;
        var metrics = VM.get_guest_metrics(session, vm);
        return metrics.opaque_ref != "OpaqueRef:NULL"
               && VM_guest_metrics.get_PV_drivers_detected(session, metrics.opaque_ref);
    }

    var deadline = DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(timeoutSeconds);
    while (!Ready())
    {
        if (DateTime.UtcNow > deadline)
            throw new Exception($"the guest's PV drivers did not report in within {timeoutSeconds}s; " +
                "does the source VM have a guest OS with PV drivers (XenServer VM Tools)?");
        System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(intervalSeconds * 1000);
    }
}

/// <summary>Merge CLI-supplied overrides onto a workflow's dispatcher defaults.</summary>
private static Dictionary<string, string> Merge(Dictionary<string, string> defaults,
    Dictionary<string, string> overrides)
{
    var result = new Dictionary<string, string>(defaults);
    foreach (var kv in overrides) result[kv.Key] = kv.Value;
    return result;
}
```

## Python

```python
def connect(url, username, password):
    """Open a session, skipping certificate validation for the host's self-signed cert.

    If url points at a pool *member* rather than the coordinator, login fails with HOST_IS_SLAVE
    naming the coordinator's address; we reconnect to it (assuming the coordinator is up), exactly
    as XenCenter does when you add a member server."""
    session = XenAPI.Session(url, ignore_ssl=True)
    try:
        session.login_with_password(username, password, "1.0", "sdk-examples")
    except XenAPI.Failure as e:
        if e.details[0] != "HOST_IS_SLAVE":
            raise
        session = XenAPI.Session("https://%s" % e.details[1], ignore_ssl=True)  # the coordinator
        session.login_with_password(username, password, "1.0", "sdk-examples")
    return session


def template_by_name(session, name):
    """Find a template VM by its exact name (rather than picking an arbitrary one)."""
    for ref, r in session.xenapi.VM.get_all_records().items():
        if r["is_a_template"] and r["name_label"] == name:
            return ref
    raise RuntimeError("no template named %r was found" % name)


def vm_by_name(session, name):
    """Find a guest VM (not a template, control domain or snapshot) by its exact name."""
    for ref, r in session.xenapi.VM.get_all_records().items():
        if (not r["is_a_template"] and not r["is_control_domain"]
                and not r["is_a_snapshot"] and r["name_label"] == name):
            return ref
    raise RuntimeError("no VM named %r was found" % name)


def sr_by_name(session, name, shared=False):
    """Find an SR by its exact name (optionally requiring it to be shared)."""
    for ref, r in session.xenapi.SR.get_all_records().items():
        if r["name_label"] == name and (not shared or r["shared"]):
            return ref
    raise RuntimeError("no %sSR named %r was found" % ("shared " if shared else "", name))


def detach_and_forget_sr(session, sr):
    """Detach an SR from every host, then forget it - XenCenter's Detach followed by Forget.

    SR.forget refuses an SR that is still attached (SR_HAS_PBD), so unplug its PBDs first. Forgetting
    drops the pool's record of the SR but leaves the data on the storage itself."""
    for pbd in session.xenapi.SR.get_PBDs(sr):
        if session.xenapi.PBD.get_currently_attached(pbd):
            session.xenapi.PBD.unplug(pbd)
    session.xenapi.SR.forget(sr)


def provision(session, vm):
    """Provision a cloned template into a real VM, filling in the SR first.

    A template's other_config["disks"] is <provision><disk ... sr="" .../></provision> - sr="" means
    "whoever provisions this names the SR". VM.provision takes it literally and fails with
    UUID_INVALID, so rewrite every <disk>'s sr to the pool's default SR first, exactly as
    `xe vm-install` does, before provisioning."""
    pool_ref = session.xenapi.pool.get_all()[0]
    sr_uuid = session.xenapi.SR.get_uuid(session.xenapi.pool.get_default_SR(pool_ref))

    disks_xml = session.xenapi.VM.get_other_config(vm).get("disks")
    if disks_xml:
        root = ET.fromstring(disks_xml)
        for disk in root.findall("disk"):
            disk.set("sr", sr_uuid)
        session.xenapi.VM.remove_from_other_config(vm, "disks")
        session.xenapi.VM.add_to_other_config(vm, "disks", ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode"))

    session.xenapi.VM.provision(vm)


def copy_of_guest(session, source_vm_name, new_vm_name):
    """A throwaway VM with a working guest OS: a copy of an existing VM that has one.

    Suspend, checkpoint, live migration and clean shutdown all need the guest's cooperation: on a
    running VM with no PV drivers xapi refuses them up front with VM_LACKS_FEATURE (a VM freshly
    cloned from a template has no OS at all). So copy a VM that does have an OS and PV drivers,
    without disturbing it: snapshot it (fine while it runs), clone the snapshot - a clone of a
    snapshot is a template - and provision that into an ordinary VM. The snapshot is only needed
    for the clone, so it goes again straight away."""
    source = vm_by_name(session, source_vm_name)
    snapshot = session.xenapi.VM.snapshot(source, new_vm_name + "-source")
    vm = session.xenapi.VM.clone(snapshot, new_vm_name)
    provision(session, vm)
    destroy_vm_and_disks(session, snapshot)
    return vm


def wait_for_guest_agent(session, vm, timeout=300, interval=2):
    """Wait, after VM.start, until the guest's PV drivers have reported in.

    xapi only offers the guest-dependent operations once the guest says it can do them, and
    allowed_operations is where it says so: wait for clean_shutdown to appear there (the same
    check that refuses it with VM_LACKS_FEATURE beforehand). A Linux kernel offers that early in
    boot, before the agent runs (hot-plug needs the agent, and suspend needs its emulated disk
    unplugged), so wait for the guest metrics to report the PV drivers too. A booting OS takes a while."""
    def ready():
        if "clean_shutdown" not in session.xenapi.VM.get_allowed_operations(vm):
            return False
        metrics = session.xenapi.VM.get_guest_metrics(vm)
        return metrics != "OpaqueRef:NULL" and session.xenapi.VM_guest_metrics.get_PV_drivers_detected(metrics)

    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while not ready():
        if time.time() > deadline:
            raise RuntimeError("the guest's PV drivers did not report in within %ds; does the source "
                               "VM have a guest OS with PV drivers (XenServer VM Tools)?" % timeout)
        time.sleep(interval)


def _xml_from_failure(e):
    """The first (from the end) XenAPI.Failure detail that looks like an XML fragment, or None."""
    for detail in reversed(e.details):
        if detail and detail.lstrip().startswith("<"):
            return detail
    return None


def _probe_for_failure(session, host, device_config, sm_type):
    """Return the XML a backend sends back on its deliberately-failing discovery probe.

    The New SR wizard (and XenRT) discover iSCSI/HBA LUNs by asking with an incomplete
    device-config on purpose: the backend can't create anything from it yet, so it fails with an
    SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_<n> error whose params carry an XML fragment describing what it found (the
    IQNs on offer, then the LUNs behind one of them, or - for HBA - every LUN visible at all).
    A probe that unexpectedly *succeeds* means the device-config was already complete - not the
    discovery prompt this helper is looking for. (Never probe by attempting SR.create instead: on
    real storage a create that succeeds formats the LUN.)"""
    try:
        session.xenapi.SR.probe(host, device_config, sm_type, {})
    except XenAPI.Failure as e:
        xml = _xml_from_failure(e)
        if xml:
            return xml
        raise
    raise RuntimeError("SR.probe for %s succeeded without asking for more information; "
                       "check the target address" % sm_type)


def _choose_target_iqn(iqn_xml, target, target_iqn):
    """Pick the IQN from an iSCSI discovery probe: the caller's, if named (it must be one the target
    offers), else the first. An array usually offers many targets - one per LUN, often belonging to
    different users - so on shared storage always name yours: SR.create formats the LUN behind it."""
    offered = [e.text for e in iqn_xml.findall(".//TargetIQN")]
    if target_iqn and target_iqn not in offered:
        raise RuntimeError("target %s does not offer IQN %s" % (target, target_iqn))
    return target_iqn or offered[0]


def _self_signed_cert_pem():
    """A throwaway self-signed certificate and private key (PEM), the way XenRT provisions one for
    its own certificate tests.

    Prefers the `cryptography` package (pure Python, no external tool needed) when it's installed;
    falls back to shelling out to `openssl req -x509` - the same tool XenRT itself uses - when it
    isn't, so this works either way without forcing an extra dependency on everyone."""
    try:
        import datetime
        from cryptography import x509
        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes, serialization
        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
        from cryptography.x509.oid import NameOID

        key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
        name = x509.Name([x509.NameAttribute(NameOID.COMMON_NAME, "sdk-example")])
        now = datetime.datetime.utcnow()
        cert = (x509.CertificateBuilder()
                .subject_name(name).issuer_name(name).public_key(key.public_key())
                .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
                .not_valid_before(now - datetime.timedelta(days=1))
                .not_valid_after(now + datetime.timedelta(days=365))
                .sign(key, hashes.SHA256()))
        cert_pem = cert.public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM).decode()
        key_pem = key.private_bytes(
            serialization.Encoding.PEM, serialization.PrivateFormat.TraditionalOpenSSL,
            serialization.NoEncryption()).decode()
        return cert_pem, key_pem
    except ImportError:
        handle, keypath = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="sdk-example-key-", suffix=".pem")
        os.close(handle)
        handle, certpath = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="sdk-example-cert-", suffix=".pem")
        os.close(handle)
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                ["openssl", "req", "-x509", "-newkey", "rsa:2048", "-nodes",
                 "-keyout", keypath, "-out", certpath, "-days", "365", "-subj", "/CN=sdk-example"],
                check=True, capture_output=True)
            with open(certpath) as f:
                cert_pem = f.read()
            with open(keypath) as f:
                key_pem = f.read()
            return cert_pem, key_pem
        finally:
            os.remove(keypath)
            os.remove(certpath)


def _reconnect_after_master_change(url, username, password, new_master_uuid, timeout=600, interval=5):
    """Wait out a pool-wide xapi restart (pool.designate_new_master) and reconnect.

    designate_new_master returns BEFORE the change: for a while the old coordinator still answers,
    and still says it is the coordinator, until xapi restarts across the pool. So reconnecting is not
    enough - keep reconnecting until the pool names the new coordinator (by uuid; connect() follows
    HOST_IS_SLAVE to wherever the coordinator now is). XenRT's own helper likewise waits minutes
    before trusting the pool again."""
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    last_error = None
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            session = connect(url, username, password)
            x = session.xenapi
            master = x.pool.get_master(x.pool.get_all()[0])
            # The new coordinator answers before the pool has settled - calls made too soon fail
            # (HANDLE_INVALID on the operation's own task) - so also wait for every host to be back,
            # live and enabled.
            if x.host.get_uuid(master) == new_master_uuid and all(
                    r["enabled"] and x.host_metrics.get_live(r["metrics"])
                    for r in x.host.get_all_records().values()):
                return session
            x.session.logout()
            last_error = "the pool has not settled under the new coordinator"
        except Exception as e:
            last_error = e
        time.sleep(interval)
    raise RuntimeError("the pool did not come back after the master change: %s" % last_error)


def _wait_for_host_live(x, host, want, timeout=60, interval=2):
    """Poll host_metrics.live until it matches, rather than issuing the next power command
    immediately - real out-of-band power control has no retry of its own, so a tool that doesn't
    wait can issue a second command while the first is still in flight."""
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while host_live(x, host) != want:
        if time.time() > deadline:
            raise RuntimeError("host did not reach live=%s in time" % want)
        time.sleep(interval)


def _wait_for_restart(url, username, password, host_uuid, key, before, timeout=1800, interval=10):
    """Wait for a host to come back from a reboot (key "boot_time") or toolstack restart
    ("agent_start_time"): until that other_config entry differs from `before` and the host is live.
    Reconnects every time round, because the host restarting may be the coordinator this session
    talks to; returns the new session."""
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while True:
        try:
            session = connect(url, username, password)
            x = session.xenapi
            host = x.host.get_by_uuid(host_uuid)
            if x.host.get_other_config(host).get(key) != before and host_live(x, host):
                return session
            x.session.logout()
        except (OSError, xmlrpc.client.ProtocolError, XenAPI.Failure):
            pass                     # down, or xapi still starting
        if time.time() > deadline:
            raise RuntimeError("host %s did not come back in time" % host_uuid)
        time.sleep(interval)


def _enable_when_booted(x, host, timeout=600, interval=10):
    """Re-enable a host that has just come back. It reports itself live before xapi on it has
    finished starting, and until then host.enable fails HOST_STILL_BOOTING - so retry that."""
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while True:
        try:
            x.host.enable(host)
            return
        except XenAPI.Failure as e:
            if e.details[0] != "HOST_STILL_BOOTING" or time.time() > deadline:
                raise
            time.sleep(interval)


def _host_url(url, address):
    """Build the URL for a given host's own address, keeping the scheme and port the caller
    originally connected with (a host's management address carries no port of its own)."""
    parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
    port = ":%d" % parts.port if parts.port else ""
    return "%s://%s%s" % (parts.scheme, address, port)


def _move_disks_to_sr(session, vm, sr_ref):
    """Relocate every one of a (not-yet-started) VM's disks onto the given SR, the same
    VDI.pool_migrate storage-migrate already demonstrates."""
    for vdi in _disk_vdis(session, vm):
        if session.xenapi.VDI.get_SR(vdi) != sr_ref:
            session.xenapi.VDI.pool_migrate(vdi, sr_ref, {})
```

```java
private static Connection connect(String url, String user, String password) throws Exception {
    CloseableHttpClient http = trustingHttpClient();
    try {
        return login(http, url, user, password);
    } catch (Types.HostIsSlave e) {
        // A pool member names the coordinator's address; reconnect there (assuming the coordinator
        // is up), exactly as XenCenter does when you add a member server.
        return login(http, "https://" + e.masterIPAddress, user, password);
    }
}

// An HTTP client that trusts the host's self-signed certificate. (Apache HttpClient 5 uses its own
// SSL context, so we configure it here rather than relying on JVM-wide defaults.)
private static CloseableHttpClient trustingHttpClient() throws Exception {
    SSLContext ssl = SSLContexts.custom()
        .loadTrustMaterial((chain, authType) -> true)
        .build();
    SSLConnectionSocketFactory sslsf = new SSLConnectionSocketFactory(ssl, NoopHostnameVerifier.INSTANCE);
    PoolingHttpClientConnectionManager cm = PoolingHttpClientConnectionManagerBuilder.create()
        .setSSLSocketFactory(sslsf)
        .build();
    return HttpClients.custom().setConnectionManager(cm).build();
}

private static Connection login(CloseableHttpClient http, String url, String user, String password) throws Exception {
    Connection conn = new Connection(new JsonRpcClient(http, new URL(url + "/jsonrpc")));
    Session.loginWithPassword(conn, user, password, "1.0", "sdk-examples");
    return conn;
}

// Look up a template VM by its exact name (rather than picking an arbitrary one).
private static VM templateByName(Connection conn, String name) throws Exception {
    for (Map.Entry<VM, VM.Record> e : VM.getAllRecords(conn).entrySet())
        if (e.getValue().isATemplate && name.equals(e.getValue().nameLabel)) return e.getKey();
    throw new RuntimeException("no template named '" + name + "' was found");
}

// Look up a guest VM (not a template, control domain or snapshot) by its exact name.
private static VM vmByName(Connection conn, String name) throws Exception {
    for (Map.Entry<VM, VM.Record> e : VM.getAllRecords(conn).entrySet()) {
        VM.Record r = e.getValue();
        if (!r.isATemplate && !r.isControlDomain && !r.isASnapshot && name.equals(r.nameLabel))
            return e.getKey();
    }
    throw new RuntimeException("no VM named '" + name + "' was found");
}

// Look up an SR by its exact name (optionally requiring it to be shared).
private static SR srByName(Connection conn, String name, boolean shared) throws Exception {
    for (Map.Entry<SR, SR.Record> e : SR.getAllRecords(conn).entrySet())
        if (name.equals(e.getValue().nameLabel) && (!shared || e.getValue().shared)) return e.getKey();
    throw new RuntimeException("no " + (shared ? "shared " : "") + "SR named '" + name + "' was found");
}

// The VDIs backing a VM's disk VBDs (used to clean up a clone/copy/created VM's disks). VM.destroy
// leaves VDIs behind, so callers destroy these explicitly afterward.
private static Set<VDI> diskVdis(Connection conn, VM vm) throws Exception {
    Set<VDI> vdis = new LinkedHashSet<>();
    for (VBD vbd : vm.getVBDs(conn))
        if (vbd.getType(conn) == Types.VbdType.DISK) vdis.add(vbd.getVDI(conn));
    return vdis;
}

// VM.destroy removes the VM record but leaves its disks behind; collect the owned VDIs first and
// destroy them afterward. Works for a snapshot/checkpoint too - its "disks" are its own snapshot VDIs.
private static void destroyVmAndDisks(Connection conn, VM vm) throws Exception {
    Set<VDI> vdis = new LinkedHashSet<>(diskVdis(conn, vm));
    // A checkpoint (or a suspended VM) also owns a suspend image holding its memory, which no VBD
    // points at: destroy that as well.
    VDI suspendVdi = vm.getSuspendVDI(conn);
    if (!suspendVdi.toWireString().equals("OpaqueRef:NULL")) vdis.add(suspendVdi);
    vm.destroy(conn);
    for (VDI vdi : vdis) vdi.destroy(conn);
}

// Detach an SR from every host, then forget it: XenCenter's Detach followed by Forget. SR.forget refuses
// an SR that is still attached (SR_HAS_PBD), so unplug its PBDs first. Forgetting drops the pool's record
// of the SR but leaves the data on the storage itself.
private static void detachAndForgetSr(Connection conn, SR sr) throws Exception {
    for (PBD pbd : sr.getPBDs(conn)) {
        if (pbd.getCurrentlyAttached(conn)) pbd.unplug(conn);
    }
    sr.forget(conn);
}

// What xe vm-install does before VM.provision: a template's other_config["disks"] names sr="" for
// every disk, and released xapi takes that literally and fails with UUID_INVALID. Rewrite each
// disk's sr attribute to the pool's default SR first.
private static void provision(Connection conn, VM vm) throws Exception {
    String disks = vm.getOtherConfig(conn).get("disks");
    if (disks != null && disks.contains("sr=\"\"")) {
        SR defaultSr = Pool.getAllRecords(conn).values().iterator().next().defaultSR;
        vm.removeFromOtherConfig(conn, "disks");
        vm.addToOtherConfig(conn, "disks", disks.replace("sr=\"\"", "sr=\"" + defaultSr.getUuid(conn) + "\""));
    }
    vm.provision(conn);
}

// The first (from the end) field of a probe failure that looks like an XML fragment, or null.
// SR.probe's deliberate failures surface as SrBackendFailure (status/stdout/stderr); other XenAPI
// failures carry their raw params in errorDescription. Scan in reverse, like the Python reference.
private static String xmlFromFailure(Types.XenAPIException e) {
    java.util.List<String> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
    if (e instanceof Types.SrBackendFailure) {
        Types.SrBackendFailure sbf = (Types.SrBackendFailure) e;
        candidates.add(sbf.status);
        candidates.add(sbf.stdout);
        candidates.add(sbf.stderr);
    } else if (e.errorDescription != null) {
        candidates.addAll(java.util.Arrays.asList(e.errorDescription));
    }
    java.util.Collections.reverse(candidates);
    for (String c : candidates) {
        if (c != null && c.trim().startsWith("<")) return c;
    }
    return null;
}

// Return the XML a backend sends back on its deliberately-failing discovery probe. The New SR
// wizard (and XenRT) discover iSCSI/HBA LUNs by asking with an incomplete device-config on purpose:
// the backend can't create anything from it yet, so it fails with an SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_<n> error
// whose params carry an XML fragment describing what it found. A probe that unexpectedly SUCCEEDS
// means the device-config was already complete - not the discovery prompt this helper looks for.
// Never probe by attempting SR.create instead: on real storage a create that succeeds formats the LUN.
private static String probeForFailure(Connection conn, Host host, Map<String, String> deviceConfig,
        String smType) throws Exception {
    try {
        SR.probe(conn, host, deviceConfig, smType, new HashMap<String, String>());
    } catch (Types.XenAPIException e) {
        String xml = xmlFromFailure(e);
        if (xml != null) return xml;
        throw e;
    }
    throw new RuntimeException("SR.probe for " + smType + " succeeded without asking for more "
            + "information; check the target address");
}

// Parse an XML fragment and return its document root (used on the probe XML above).
private static org.w3c.dom.Document parseXml(String xml) throws Exception {
    return javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance().newDocumentBuilder()
            .parse(new org.xml.sax.InputSource(new java.io.StringReader(xml)));
}

private static String firstTagText(org.w3c.dom.Element root, String tag) {
    org.w3c.dom.NodeList nodes = root.getElementsByTagName(tag);
    return nodes.getLength() > 0 ? nodes.item(0).getTextContent() : null;
}

// Pick the IQN from an iSCSI discovery probe: the caller's, if named (it must be one the target
// offers), else the first. An array usually offers many targets - one per LUN, often belonging to
// different users - so on shared storage always name yours: SR.create formats the LUN behind it.
private static String chooseTargetIqn(org.w3c.dom.Element iqnRoot, String target, String targetIqn) {
    org.w3c.dom.NodeList nodes = iqnRoot.getElementsByTagName("TargetIQN");
    List<String> offered = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int i = 0; i < nodes.getLength(); i++) offered.add(nodes.item(i).getTextContent());
    if (targetIqn == null || targetIqn.isEmpty()) return offered.get(0);
    if (!offered.contains(targetIqn))
        throw new RuntimeException("target " + target + " does not offer IQN " + targetIqn);
    return targetIqn;
}

// A throwaway self-signed certificate and private key (PEM), the way XenRT provisions one for its
// own certificate tests. Java has no dependency-free public API to mint an X.509 certificate (the
// internal sun.security.x509 classes need extra JVM flags under the module system), so shell out to
// openssl - the same tool XenRT itself uses - and read the two PEM files back.
private static String[] selfSignedCertPem() throws Exception {
    java.io.File keyFile = java.io.File.createTempFile("sdk-example-key-", ".pem");
    java.io.File certFile = java.io.File.createTempFile("sdk-example-cert-", ".pem");
    try {
        Process p = new ProcessBuilder("openssl", "req", "-x509", "-newkey", "rsa:2048", "-nodes",
                "-keyout", keyFile.getAbsolutePath(), "-out", certFile.getAbsolutePath(),
                "-days", "365", "-subj", "/CN=sdk-example")
                .redirectErrorStream(true).start();
        String output = new String(p.getInputStream().readAllBytes(), java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        int code = p.waitFor();
        if (code != 0) throw new RuntimeException("openssl failed (" + code + "): " + output);
        String certPem = java.nio.file.Files.readString(certFile.toPath());
        String keyPem = java.nio.file.Files.readString(keyFile.toPath());
        return new String[]{certPem, keyPem};
    } finally {
        keyFile.delete();
        certFile.delete();
    }
}

// Wait out a pool-wide xapi restart (pool.designateNewMaster) and reconnect.
//
// designateNewMaster returns BEFORE the change: for a while the old coordinator still answers, and
// still says it is the coordinator, until xapi restarts across the pool. So reconnecting is not
// enough - keep reconnecting until the pool names the new coordinator (by uuid; connect() follows
// HOST_IS_SLAVE to wherever the coordinator now is). XenRT's own helper likewise waits minutes before
// trusting the pool again.
private static Connection reconnectAfterMasterChange(String url, String user, String password,
        String newMasterUuid) throws Exception {
    long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + 600_000;
    Object lastError = null;
    while (System.currentTimeMillis() < deadline) {
        try {
            Connection conn = connect(url, user, password);
            Host master = Pool.getAll(conn).iterator().next().getMaster(conn);
            // The new coordinator answers before the pool has settled - calls made too soon fail
            // (HANDLE_INVALID on the operation's own task) - so also wait for every host to be back,
            // live and enabled.
            boolean settled = master.getUuid(conn).equals(newMasterUuid);
            if (settled) {
                for (Map.Entry<Host, Host.Record> e : Host.getAllRecords(conn).entrySet()) {
                    if (!e.getValue().enabled || !e.getValue().metrics.getLive(conn)) {
                        settled = false;
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (settled) return conn;
            Session.logout(conn);
            lastError = "the pool has not settled under the new coordinator";
        } catch (Exception e) {
            lastError = e;
        }
        Thread.sleep(5000);
    }
    throw new RuntimeException("the pool did not come back after the master change: " + lastError);
}

// Poll host_metrics.live until it matches, rather than issuing the next power command immediately -
// real out-of-band power control has no retry of its own, so a tool that doesn't wait can issue a
// second command while the first is still in flight.
private static void waitForHostLive(Connection conn, Host host, boolean want) throws Exception {
    waitForHostLive(conn, host, want, 60_000, 2000);
}

private static void waitForHostLive(Connection conn, Host host, boolean want, long timeoutMillis,
        long intervalMillis) throws Exception {
    long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + timeoutMillis;
    while (host.getMetrics(conn).getLive(conn) != want) {
        if (System.currentTimeMillis() > deadline)
            throw new RuntimeException("host did not reach live=" + want + " in time");
        Thread.sleep(intervalMillis);
    }
}

// Re-enable a host that has just come back. It reports itself live before xapi on it has finished
// starting, and until then host.enable fails HOST_STILL_BOOTING - so retry that.
private static void enableWhenBooted(Connection conn, Host host) throws Exception {
    long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + 600_000;
    while (true) {
        try {
            host.enable(conn);
            return;
        } catch (Types.HostStillBooting e) {
            if (System.currentTimeMillis() > deadline) throw e;
            Thread.sleep(10_000);
        }
    }
}

// Wait for a host to come back from a reboot (key "boot_time") or toolstack restart
// ("agent_start_time"): until that other_config entry differs from `before` and the host is live.
// Reconnects every time round, because the host restarting may be the coordinator this connection
// talks to; returns the new Connection.
private static Connection waitForRestart(String url, String user, String password, String hostUuid,
        String key, String before) throws Exception {
    long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + 1_800_000;
    while (true) {
        try {
            Connection conn = connect(url, user, password);
            Host host = Host.getByUuid(conn, hostUuid);
            String now = host.getOtherConfig(conn).get(key);
            if (!java.util.Objects.equals(now, before) && host.getMetrics(conn).getLive(conn)) return conn;
            Session.logout(conn);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            // down, or xapi still starting
        }
        if (System.currentTimeMillis() > deadline)
            throw new RuntimeException("host " + hostUuid + " did not come back in time");
        Thread.sleep(10_000);
    }
}

// Build the URL for a given host's own address, keeping the scheme and port the caller originally
// connected with (a host's management address carries no port of its own).
private static String hostUrl(String url, String address) throws Exception {
    URL parsed = new URL(url);
    int port = parsed.getPort();
    return parsed.getProtocol() + "://" + address + (port >= 0 ? ":" + port : "");
}

// Relocate every one of a (not-yet-started) VM's disks onto the given SR, the same VDI.poolMigrate
// storage-migrate already demonstrates.
private static void moveDisksToSr(Connection conn, VM vm, SR sr) throws Exception {
    for (VDI vdi : diskVdis(conn, vm)) {
        if (!vdi.getSR(conn).equals(sr)) awaitTask(conn, vdi.poolMigrateAsync(conn, sr, new HashMap<String, String>()));
    }
}

// Wait for an Async task to finish, return its result and destroy it. A call that copies a disk runs
// for many minutes - longer than the client waits for a reply (10 minutes by default) - so long
// operations start the Async twin, which returns a Task at once, and poll that instead.
private static String awaitTask(Connection conn, Task task) throws Exception {
    try {
        while (task.getStatus(conn) == Types.TaskStatusType.PENDING) Thread.sleep(1000);
        if (task.getStatus(conn) != Types.TaskStatusType.SUCCESS)
            throw new RuntimeException(task.getNameLabel(conn) + " failed: " + task.getErrorInfo(conn));
        return task.getResult(conn).replace("<value>", "").replace("</value>", "").trim();
    } finally {
        task.destroy(conn);
    }
}

// A throwaway VM with a working guest OS: a copy of an existing VM that has one. Suspend,
// checkpoint, live migration and clean shutdown all need the guest's cooperation: on a running VM
// with no PV drivers xapi refuses them up front with VM_LACKS_FEATURE (a VM freshly cloned from a
// template has no OS at all). So copy a VM that does have an OS and PV drivers, without disturbing
// it: snapshot it (fine while it runs), clone the snapshot - a clone of a snapshot is a template -
// and provision that into an ordinary VM. The snapshot is only needed for the clone, so it goes
// again straight away.
private static VM copyOfGuest(Connection conn, String sourceVmName, String newVmName) throws Exception {
    VM source = vmByName(conn, sourceVmName);
    VM snapshot = source.snapshot(conn, newVmName + "-source");
    VM vm = snapshot.createClone(conn, newVmName);
    provision(conn, vm);
    destroyVmAndDisks(conn, snapshot);
    return vm;
}

// Wait, after VM.start, until the guest's PV drivers have reported in. xapi only offers the
// guest-dependent operations once the guest says it can do them, and getAllowedOperations is where
// it says so: wait for CLEAN_SHUTDOWN to appear there (the same check that refuses it with
// VM_LACKS_FEATURE beforehand). A booting OS takes a while.
// clean_shutdown in allowed_operations says the guest can shut down; a Linux kernel offers that early in
// boot, before the agent runs (hot-plug needs the agent, and suspend needs its emulated disk unplugged),
// so wait for the guest metrics to report the PV drivers too.
private static boolean guestAgentReady(Connection conn, VM vm) throws Exception {
    if (!vm.getAllowedOperations(conn).contains(Types.VmOperations.CLEAN_SHUTDOWN)) return false;
    VMGuestMetrics metrics = vm.getGuestMetrics(conn);
    return !metrics.toWireString().equals("OpaqueRef:NULL") && metrics.getPVDriversDetected(conn);
}

private static void waitForGuestAgent(Connection conn, VM vm) throws Exception {
    waitForGuestAgent(conn, vm, 300, 2);
}

private static void waitForGuestAgent(Connection conn, VM vm, int timeoutSeconds, int intervalSeconds)
        throws Exception {
    long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + timeoutSeconds * 1000L;
    while (!guestAgentReady(conn, vm)) {
        if (System.currentTimeMillis() > deadline)
            throw new RuntimeException("the guest's PV drivers did not report in within " + timeoutSeconds
                    + "s; does the source VM have a guest OS with PV drivers (XenServer VM Tools)?");
        Thread.sleep(intervalSeconds * 1000L);
    }
}
```
