## Go

```go
func connect(url, user, password string) *xenapi.Session {
	session, err := login(url, user, password)
	if err == nil {
		return session
	}
	// A pool member names the coordinator's address; reconnect there (assuming the coordinator is up),
	// exactly as XenCenter does when you add a member server.
	coordinator := coordinatorFromSlaveError(err)
	if coordinator == "" {
		panic(err)
	}
	session, err = login("https://"+coordinator, user, password)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return session
}

func login(url, user, password string) (*xenapi.Session, error) {
	session := xenapi.NewSession(&xenapi.ClientOpts{URL: url})
	_, err := session.LoginWithPassword(user, password, "1.0", "sdk-examples")
	return session, err
}

// coordinatorFromSlaveError returns the coordinator address carried by a HOST_IS_SLAVE error, or "".
// The Go binding surfaces API errors as a formatted string, rendering the error's data slice (the full
// XenAPI description, [code, ...params]) as "data [HOST_IS_SLAVE <addr>]" - so we recognise the code and
// take the address, which is the last element of that slice.
func coordinatorFromSlaveError(err error) string {
	msg := err.Error()
	if !strings.Contains(msg, xenapi.ErrorHostIsSlave) {
		return ""
	}
	if m := regexp.MustCompile(`data \[(.+)\]`).FindStringSubmatch(msg); m != nil {
		if fields := strings.Fields(m[1]); len(fields) > 0 {
			return fields[len(fields)-1]
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func check(err error) {
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}

// templateByName finds a template VM by its exact name (rather than picking an arbitrary one).
func templateByName(session *xenapi.Session, name string) xenapi.VMRef {
	vms, err := xenapi.VM.GetAllRecords(session)
	check(err)
	for ref, vm := range vms {
		if vm.IsATemplate && vm.NameLabel == name {
			return ref
		}
	}
	panic(fmt.Sprintf("no template named %q was found", name))
}

// vmByName finds a guest VM (not a template, control domain or snapshot) by its exact name.
func vmByName(session *xenapi.Session, name string) xenapi.VMRef {
	vms, err := xenapi.VM.GetAllRecords(session)
	check(err)
	for ref, vm := range vms {
		if !vm.IsATemplate && !vm.IsControlDomain && !vm.IsASnapshot && vm.NameLabel == name {
			return ref
		}
	}
	panic(fmt.Sprintf("no VM named %q was found", name))
}

// srByName finds an SR by its exact name (optionally requiring it to be shared).
func srByName(session *xenapi.Session, name string, shared bool) xenapi.SRRef {
	srs, err := xenapi.SR.GetAllRecords(session)
	check(err)
	for ref, sr := range srs {
		if sr.NameLabel == name && (!shared || sr.Shared) {
			return ref
		}
	}
	panic(fmt.Sprintf("no SR named %q was found", name))
}

// detachAndForgetSR detaches an SR from every host, then forgets it: XenCenter's Detach followed by
// Forget. SR.Forget refuses an SR that is still attached (SR_HAS_PBD), so unplug its PBDs first.
// Forgetting drops the pool's record of the SR but leaves the data on the storage itself.
func detachAndForgetSR(session *xenapi.Session, sr xenapi.SRRef) {
	pbds, err := xenapi.SR.GetPBDs(session, sr)
	check(err)
	for _, pbd := range pbds {
		attached, err := xenapi.PBD.GetCurrentlyAttached(session, pbd)
		check(err)
		if attached {
			check(xenapi.PBD.Unplug(session, pbd))
		}
	}
	check(xenapi.SR.Forget(session, sr))
}

// provision is VM.Provision, after filling in the SR for every disk the template describes. A template's
// other_config["disks"] names each disk's SR as sr="" (empty); a real host takes that literally and
// VM.Provision fails with UUID_INVALID, so point the disks at the pool's default SR first - exactly what
// `xe vm-install` does before calling VM.provision itself.
func provision(session *xenapi.Session, vm xenapi.VMRef) {
	otherConfig, err := xenapi.VM.GetOtherConfig(session, vm)
	check(err)
	if disks, ok := otherConfig["disks"]; ok && strings.Contains(disks, `sr=""`) {
		pools, err := xenapi.Pool.GetAll(session)
		check(err)
		defaultSR, err := xenapi.Pool.GetDefaultSR(session, pools[0])
		check(err)
		srUUID, err := xenapi.SR.GetUUID(session, defaultSR)
		check(err)
		check(xenapi.VM.RemoveFromOtherConfig(session, vm, "disks"))
		check(xenapi.VM.AddToOtherConfig(session, vm, "disks", strings.ReplaceAll(disks, `sr=""`, `sr="`+srUUID+`"`)))
	}
	check(xenapi.VM.Provision(session, vm))
}

// copyOfGuest makes a throwaway VM with a working guest OS: a copy of an existing VM that has one.
//
// Suspend, checkpoint, live migration and clean shutdown all need the guest's cooperation: on a
// running VM with no PV drivers xapi refuses them up front with VM_LACKS_FEATURE (a VM freshly
// cloned from a template has no OS at all). So copy a VM that does have an OS and PV drivers,
// without disturbing it: snapshot it (fine while it runs), clone the snapshot - a clone of a
// snapshot is a template - and provision that into an ordinary VM. The snapshot is only needed for
// the clone, so it goes again straight away.
func copyOfGuest(session *xenapi.Session, sourceVMName, newVMName string) xenapi.VMRef {
	source := vmByName(session, sourceVMName)
	snapshot, err := xenapi.VM.Snapshot(session, source, newVMName+"-source", nil)
	check(err)
	vm, err := xenapi.VM.Clone(session, snapshot, newVMName)
	check(err)
	provision(session, vm)
	destroyVMAndDisks(session, snapshot)
	return vm
}

// waitForGuestAgent waits, after VM.Start, until the guest's PV drivers have reported in.
//
// xapi only offers the guest-dependent operations once the guest says it can do them, and
// allowed_operations is where it says so: wait for clean_shutdown to appear there (the same check
// that refuses it with VM_LACKS_FEATURE beforehand). A booting OS takes a while.
// guestAgentReady: clean_shutdown in allowed_operations says the guest can shut down; a Linux kernel offers
// that early in boot, before the agent runs (hot-plug needs the agent, and suspend needs its emulated disk
// unplugged), so the guest metrics must report the PV drivers too.
func guestAgentReady(session *xenapi.Session, vm xenapi.VMRef) bool {
	ops, err := xenapi.VM.GetAllowedOperations(session, vm)
	check(err)
	canShutDown := false
	for _, op := range ops {
		canShutDown = canShutDown || op == xenapi.VMOperationsCleanShutdown
	}
	if !canShutDown {
		return false
	}
	metrics, err := xenapi.VM.GetGuestMetrics(session, vm)
	check(err)
	if metrics == xenapi.VMGuestMetricsRef("OpaqueRef:NULL") {
		return false
	}
	detected, err := xenapi.VMGuestMetrics.GetPVDriversDetected(session, metrics)
	check(err)
	return detected
}

func waitForGuestAgent(session *xenapi.Session, vm xenapi.VMRef) {
	const timeout = 300 * time.Second
	const interval = 2 * time.Second
	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
	for {
		if guestAgentReady(session, vm) {
			return
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("the guest's PV drivers did not report in within %s; does the source "+
				"VM have a guest OS with PV drivers (XenServer VM Tools)?", timeout))
		}
		time.Sleep(interval)
	}
}

// probeForFailure runs SR.probe's deliberately-incomplete discovery call and returns the XML
// fragment its failure carries describing what it found. The New SR wizard (and XenRT) discover
// iSCSI/HBA LUNs by asking with an incomplete device-config on purpose: the backend can't create
// anything from it yet, so it fails with an error whose params carry an XML fragment describing
// what it found. A probe that unexpectedly succeeds means the device-config was already complete -
// not the discovery prompt this helper is looking for. Never fall back to SR.create instead: on
// real storage a create that unexpectedly succeeds formats the LUN.
func probeForFailure(session *xenapi.Session, host xenapi.HostRef, deviceConfig map[string]string, smType string) string {
	_, err := xenapi.SR.Probe(session, host, deviceConfig, smType, map[string]string{})
	if err == nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("SR.probe for %s succeeded without asking for more information; "+
			"check the target address", smType))
	}
	if xml := xmlFromFailure(err); xml != "" {
		return xml
	}
	panic(err)
}

// xmlFromFailure pulls the XML fragment out of a XenAPI failure's text. The Go binding renders an
// API error as a formatted string ending "... data [<code> <param> <param> ...]" (see
// coordinatorFromSlaveError) rather than keeping the params as separate values, so splitting on
// whitespace would break up the XML itself wherever it contains one. The XML fragment is always
// the last parameter in these errors, so take everything from the first "<" onward instead.
func xmlFromFailure(err error) string {
	msg := err.Error()
	i := strings.Index(msg, "data [")
	if i < 0 {
		return ""
	}
	inner := strings.TrimSuffix(msg[i+len("data ["):], "]")
	if j := strings.Index(inner, "<"); j >= 0 {
		return inner[j:]
	}
	return ""
}

// selfSignedCertPEM generates a throwaway self-signed certificate and private key (PEM), the way
// XenRT provisions one for its own certificate tests. Go's standard library crypto/x509 and
// crypto/rsa need no external tool for this, unlike some other languages here.
func selfSignedCertPEM() (certPEM, keyPEM string) {
	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	check(err)
	template := x509.Certificate{
		SerialNumber: big.NewInt(time.Now().UnixNano()),
		Subject:      pkix.Name{CommonName: "sdk-example"},
		NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour),
		NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(365 * 24 * time.Hour),
	}
	der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, &template, &template, &key.PublicKey, key)
	check(err)
	certPEM = string(pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "CERTIFICATE", Bytes: der}))
	keyPEM = string(pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "RSA PRIVATE KEY", Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PrivateKey(key)}))
	return
}

// reconnectAfterMasterChange waits out a pool-wide xapi restart (pool.DesignateNewMaster) and
// reconnects.
//
// DesignateNewMaster returns BEFORE the change: for a while the old coordinator still answers, and
// still says it is the coordinator, until xapi restarts across the pool. So reconnecting is not
// enough - keep reconnecting until the pool names the new coordinator (by uuid; connect follows
// HOST_IS_SLAVE to wherever the coordinator now is). XenRT's own helper likewise waits minutes
// before trusting the pool again.
func reconnectAfterMasterChange(url, user, password, newMasterUUID string) (session *xenapi.Session) {
	deadline := time.Now().Add(600 * time.Second)
	var lastErr any
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		settled := func() (ok bool) {
			defer func() {
				if r := recover(); r != nil {
					lastErr = r
					ok = false
				}
			}()
			session = connect(url, user, password)
			pools, err := xenapi.Pool.GetAll(session)
			check(err)
			master, err := xenapi.Pool.GetMaster(session, pools[0])
			check(err)
			uuid, err := xenapi.Host.GetUUID(session, master)
			check(err)
			// The new coordinator answers before the pool has settled - calls made too soon fail
			// (HANDLE_INVALID on the operation's own task) - so also wait for every host to be back,
			// live and enabled.
			if uuid != newMasterUUID {
				lastErr = "the pool has not settled under the new coordinator"
				return false
			}
			hosts, err := xenapi.Host.GetAllRecords(session)
			check(err)
			for _, h := range hosts {
				live, err := xenapi.HostMetrics.GetLive(session, h.Metrics)
				check(err)
				if !h.Enabled || !live {
					lastErr = "the pool has not settled under the new coordinator"
					return false
				}
			}
			return true
		}()
		if settled {
			return session
		}
		if session != nil {
			session.Logout()
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
	}
	panic(fmt.Sprintf("the pool did not come back after the master change: %v", lastErr))
}

// waitForHostLive polls host_metrics.live until it matches, rather than issuing the next power
// command immediately - real out-of-band power control has no retry of its own, so a tool that
// doesn't wait can issue a second command while the first is still in flight.
func waitForHostLive(session *xenapi.Session, host xenapi.HostRef, want bool) {
	waitForHostLiveTimeout(session, host, want, 60*time.Second, 2*time.Second)
}

func waitForHostLiveTimeout(session *xenapi.Session, host xenapi.HostRef, want bool, timeout, interval time.Duration) {
	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
	for hostLive(session, host) != want {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("host did not reach live=%t in time", want))
		}
		time.Sleep(interval)
	}
}

// enableWhenBooted re-enables a host that has just come back. It reports itself live before xapi
// on it has finished starting, and until then Host.Enable fails HOST_STILL_BOOTING - so retry that.
func enableWhenBooted(session *xenapi.Session, host xenapi.HostRef) {
	deadline := time.Now().Add(600 * time.Second)
	for {
		err := xenapi.Host.Enable(session, host)
		if err == nil {
			return
		}
		if failureCode(err) != xenapi.ErrorHostStillBooting || time.Now().After(deadline) {
			panic(err)
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)
	}
}

// waitForRestart waits for a host to come back from a reboot (key "boot_time") or toolstack
// restart ("agent_start_time"): until that other_config entry differs from before and the host is
// live. It reconnects every time round, because the host restarting may be the coordinator this
// session talks to; returns the new session.
func waitForRestart(url, user, password, hostUUID, key, before string) (session *xenapi.Session) {
	deadline := time.Now().Add(1800 * time.Second)
	for {
		ready := func() (ok bool) {
			defer func() {
				if recover() != nil { // down, or xapi still starting
					ok = false
				}
			}()
			session = connect(url, user, password)
			host, err := xenapi.Host.GetByUUID(session, hostUUID)
			check(err)
			otherConfig, err := xenapi.Host.GetOtherConfig(session, host)
			check(err)
			return otherConfig[key] != before && hostLive(session, host)
		}()
		if ready {
			return session
		}
		if session != nil {
			session.Logout()
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("host %s did not come back in time", hostUUID))
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)
	}
}

// hostURL rebuilds a URL for a different host's own address, keeping the original scheme and port
// (a host's management "address" field carries no port of its own). Needed anywhere a workflow
// does raw HTTP against a SPECIFIC host rather than the pool's connection URL.
func hostURL(rawURL, address string) string {
	u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
	check(err)
	host := address
	if port := u.Port(); port != "" {
		host = address + ":" + port
	}
	return u.Scheme + "://" + host
}

// moveDisksToSR relocates every one of a (not-yet-started) VM's disks onto the given SR, the same
// VDI.PoolMigrate call storage-migrate already demonstrates.
func moveDisksToSR(session *xenapi.Session, vm xenapi.VMRef, sr xenapi.SRRef) {
	for _, vdi := range diskVdis(session, vm) {
		current, err := xenapi.VDI.GetSR(session, vdi)
		check(err)
		if current != sr {
			_, err := xenapi.VDI.PoolMigrate(session, vdi, sr, map[string]string{})
			check(err)
		}
	}
}
```

## PowerShell

```powershell
function Connect-Example {
    # A thin, reusable wrapper around the connect handshake described above, so each example can stay
    # focused on the task. Follows the pool-member -> coordinator redirect (HOST_IS_SLAVE).
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Url,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$UserName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Password
    )
    # Accepting the certificate in Connect-XenServer covers the module's cmdlets, and on Windows PowerShell
    # 5.1 Invoke-RestMethod/Invoke-WebRequest as well. PowerShell 7's web cmdlets keep their own trust, so
    # extend the same acceptance to them for the examples that talk to the host over plain HTTP(S).
    if ($PSVersionTable.PSVersion.Major -ge 6) {
        $global:PSDefaultParameterValues['Invoke-RestMethod:SkipCertificateCheck'] = $true
        $global:PSDefaultParameterValues['Invoke-WebRequest:SkipCertificateCheck'] = $true
    }
    try {
        return Connect-XenServer -Url $Url -UserName $UserName -Password $Password `
            -NoWarnCertificates -NoWarnNewCertificates -SetDefaultSession -PassThru
    }
    catch {
        # A pool member reports the coordinator's address in the HOST_IS_SLAVE error; reconnect there
        # (assuming the coordinator is up, as XenCenter does when you add a member server).
        $desc = $_.Exception.ErrorDescription
        if ($desc[0] -ne "HOST_IS_SLAVE") { throw }
        return Connect-XenServer -Url "https://$($desc[1])" -UserName $UserName -Password $Password `
            -NoWarnCertificates -NoWarnNewCertificates -SetDefaultSession -PassThru
    }
}

function Invoke-XenMethod {
    # A thin JSON-RPC caller for the handful of XenAPI methods the module ships no cmdlet for (see
    # Get-XenEventBatch above for the same pattern). Pure PowerShell — Connect-Example has already trusted
    # the server's certificate, so no extra TLS setup is needed.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]$Session,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Method,
        # Optional: plenty of methods take nothing but the session (VM.get_all_records, for one), and a
        # mandatory array rejects @() rather than treating it as "no further arguments".
        [object[]]$Params = @()
    )
    $body = @{ jsonrpc = "2.0"; id = 1; method = $Method; params = @($Session.opaque_ref) + $Params } |
        ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6
    $resp = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$($Session.Url)/jsonrpc" -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"
    if ($resp.error) { throw "$Method failed: $($resp.error | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)" }
    return $resp.result
}

function Get-XenEventBatch {
    # The XenServer PowerShell module ships no event cmdlet, so this thin wrapper calls the JSON-RPC
    # event.from method directly with Invoke-RestMethod (Connect-Example has already trusted the server's
    # certificate, so no extra TLS setup is needed). An empty token returns the current
    # snapshot plus a token to watch from; passing that token back long-polls for changes.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]$Session,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string[]]$Classes,
        [string]$Token = "",
        [double]$Timeout = 5.0
    )
    $body = @{
        jsonrpc = "2.0"; id = 1; method = "event.from"
        params  = @($Session.opaque_ref, $Classes, $Token, $Timeout)
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6
    $resp = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$($Session.Url)/jsonrpc" -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"
    if ($resp.error) { throw "event.from failed: $($resp.error | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)" }
    return $resp.result
}

function Invoke-DetachAndForgetSr {
    # Detach an SR from every host, then forget it: XenCenter's Detach followed by Forget. Forget refuses an
    # SR that is still attached (SR_HAS_PBD), so unplug its PBDs first. Forgetting drops the pool's record of
    # the SR but leaves the data on the storage itself.
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Ref)
    (Get-XenSR -Ref $Ref).PBDs | ForEach-Object { Get-XenPBD -Ref $_.opaque_ref } |
        Where-Object { $_.currently_attached } |
        ForEach-Object { $_ | Invoke-XenPBD -XenAction Unplug }
    Invoke-XenSR -Ref $Ref -XenAction Forget
}

function Invoke-VmProvision {
    # Invoke-XenVM -XenAction Provision, after filling in the SR for every disk the template describes. A
    # template's other_config["disks"] names each disk's SR as sr="" (empty); a real host takes that
    # literally and Provision fails with UUID_INVALID, so point the disks at the pool's default SR first -
    # exactly what `xe vm-install` does before calling VM.provision itself.
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Ref)
    $vm = Get-XenVM -Ref $Ref
    $disks = $vm.other_config["disks"]
    if ($disks -and $disks.Contains('sr=""')) {
        $srUuid = (Get-XenSR -Ref (Get-XenPool | Select-Object -First 1).default_SR.opaque_ref).uuid
        # Set-XenVM -OtherConfig replaces the whole map, so copy it and change only "disks".
        $oc = @{}
        foreach ($k in $vm.other_config.Keys) { $oc[$k] = $vm.other_config[$k] }
        $oc["disks"] = $disks.Replace('sr=""', "sr=""$srUuid""")
        $vm | Set-XenVM -OtherConfig $oc
    }
    $vm | Invoke-XenVM -XenAction Provision
}

function Remove-VmAndDisks {
    # Destroy a VM (or snapshot, or template) an example made, and the disks it owns. Remove-XenVM removes
    # only the VM record and leaves its disks behind, so collect them first (from a fresh read of the VM:
    # an object from -PassThru may predate its disks) and destroy them afterwards - exactly what
    # Invoke-DeleteVm does by hand.
    param([Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Ref)
    $vdis = (Get-XenVM -Ref $Ref).VBDs |
        ForEach-Object { Get-XenVBD -Ref $_.opaque_ref } |
        Where-Object { $_.type -eq 'Disk' -and $_.VDI.opaque_ref -ne 'OpaqueRef:NULL' } |
        ForEach-Object { $_.VDI.opaque_ref }
    # A checkpoint (or a suspended VM) also owns a suspend image holding its memory, which no VBD points
    # at: destroy that as well.
    $suspendVdi = (Get-XenVM -Ref $Ref).suspend_VDI.opaque_ref
    if ($suspendVdi -and $suspendVdi -ne 'OpaqueRef:NULL') { $vdis = @($vdis) + $suspendVdi }
    Remove-XenVM -Ref $Ref
    $vdis | ForEach-Object { Remove-XenVDI -Ref $_ }
}

function Copy-OfGuest {
    # A throwaway VM with a working guest OS: a copy of an existing VM that has one.
    #
    # Suspend, checkpoint, live migration and clean shutdown all need the guest's cooperation: on a
    # running VM with no PV drivers xapi refuses them up front with VM_LACKS_FEATURE (a VM freshly
    # cloned from a template has no OS at all). So copy a VM that does have an OS and PV drivers,
    # without disturbing it: snapshot it (fine while it runs), clone the snapshot - a clone of a
    # snapshot is a template - and provision that into an ordinary VM. The snapshot is only needed for
    # the clone, so it goes again straight away.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$SourceVmName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$NewVmName
    )
    $source = Get-XenVM -Name $SourceVmName |
        Where-Object { -not $_.is_a_template -and -not $_.is_control_domain -and -not $_.is_a_snapshot } |
        Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $source) { throw "No VM named '$SourceVmName' was found." }
    $snapshot = $source | Invoke-XenVM -XenAction Snapshot -NewName "$NewVmName-source" -PassThru
    $vm = $snapshot | Invoke-XenVM -XenAction Clone -NewName $NewVmName -PassThru
    Invoke-VmProvision -Ref $vm.opaque_ref
    Remove-VmAndDisks -Ref $snapshot.opaque_ref
    return Get-XenVM -Ref $vm.opaque_ref
}

function Wait-GuestAgent {
    # Wait, after Start, until the guest's PV drivers have reported in.
    #
    # xapi only offers the guest-dependent operations once the guest says it can do them, and
    # allowed_operations is where it says so: wait for clean_shutdown to appear there (the same check
    # that refuses it with VM_LACKS_FEATURE beforehand). A Linux kernel offers that early in boot, before
    # the agent runs (hot-plug needs the agent, and suspend needs its emulated disk unplugged), so wait for
    # the guest metrics to report the PV drivers too. A booting OS takes a while.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Ref,
        [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 300,
        [int]$IntervalSeconds = 2
    )
    $ready = {
        $vm = Get-XenVM -Ref $Ref
        $vm.allowed_operations -contains 'clean_shutdown' -and
            $vm.guest_metrics.opaque_ref -ne 'OpaqueRef:NULL' -and
            (Get-XenVMGuestMetrics -Ref $vm.guest_metrics.opaque_ref).PV_drivers_detected
    }
    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
    while (-not (& $ready)) {
        if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) {
            throw ("the guest's PV drivers did not report in within ${TimeoutSeconds}s; does the " +
                   "source VM have a guest OS with PV drivers (XenServer VM Tools)?")
        }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds $IntervalSeconds
    }
}

function Invoke-ProbeForFailure {
    # Return the XML a backend sends back on its deliberately-failing discovery probe.
    #
    # The New SR wizard (and XenRT) discover iSCSI/HBA LUNs by asking with an incomplete device-config
    # on purpose: the backend can't create anything from it yet, so it fails with an
    # SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_<n> error whose params carry an XML fragment describing what it found (the
    # IQNs on offer, then the LUNs behind one of them, or - for HBA - every LUN visible at all). A probe
    # that unexpectedly *succeeds* means the device-config was already complete - not the discovery
    # prompt this helper is looking for. (Never probe by attempting SR.create instead: on real storage a
    # create that unexpectedly succeeds formats the LUN.)
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$XenHostRef,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][hashtable]$DeviceConfig,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$SmType
    )
    $succeeded = $false
    try {
        # SR.probe is a static call: the host goes in -XenHost, and -Ref (which the cmdlet insists on) is
        # ignored. Putting the host in -Ref instead sends an empty host, which a real host refuses with
        # HOST_OFFLINE.
        Invoke-XenSR -Ref "OpaqueRef:NULL" -XenAction Probe -XenHost $XenHostRef -DeviceConfig $DeviceConfig `
            -Type $SmType -SmConfig @{} -PassThru | Out-Null
        $succeeded = $true
    }
    catch {
        $ex = $_.Exception
        while ($ex -and -not $ex.ErrorDescription) { $ex = $ex.InnerException }
        if ($ex -and $ex.ErrorDescription) {
            for ($i = $ex.ErrorDescription.Count - 1; $i -ge 0; $i--) {
                $detail = $ex.ErrorDescription[$i]
                if ($detail -and $detail.Trim().StartsWith('<')) { return $detail }
            }
        }
        throw
    }
    if ($succeeded) {
        throw "SR.probe for $SmType succeeded without asking for more information; check the target address"
    }
}

function Select-TargetIqn {
    # Pick the IQN from an iSCSI discovery probe: the caller's, if named (it must be one the target
    # offers), else the first. An array usually offers many targets - one per LUN, often belonging to
    # different users - so on shared storage always name yours: SR.create formats the LUN behind it.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][xml]$IqnXml,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Target,
        [string]$TargetIqn
    )
    $offered = @($IqnXml.SelectNodes("//TargetIQN") | ForEach-Object { $_.InnerText })
    if (-not $TargetIqn) { return $offered[0] }
    if ($offered -notcontains $TargetIqn) { throw "target $Target does not offer IQN $TargetIqn" }
    return $TargetIqn
}

function Get-SelfSignedCertPem {
    # A throwaway self-signed certificate and private key (PEM), the way XenRT provisions one for its
    # own certificate tests. PowerShell 7 runs on .NET, which has a native crypto API for this - no
    # external tool needed (unlike PowerShell 5.1, where New-SelfSignedCertificate, or an
    # `openssl req -x509` shell-out - the same tool XenRT itself uses - would be the fallback).
    $rsa = [System.Security.Cryptography.RSA]::Create(2048)
    $req = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.CertificateRequest]::new(
        "CN=sdk-example", $rsa, [System.Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA256,
        [System.Security.Cryptography.RSASignaturePadding]::Pkcs1)
    $cert = $req.CreateSelfSigned([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddDays(-1), [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddDays(365))
    return $cert.ExportCertificatePem(), $rsa.ExportPkcs8PrivateKeyPem()
}

function Reconnect-AfterMasterChange {
    # Wait out a pool-wide xapi restart (pool.designate_new_master) and reconnect.
    #
    # designate_new_master returns BEFORE the change: for a while the old coordinator still answers,
    # and still says it is the coordinator, until xapi restarts across the pool. So reconnecting is not
    # enough - keep reconnecting until the pool names the new coordinator (by uuid; Connect-Example
    # follows HOST_IS_SLAVE to wherever the coordinator now is). XenRT's own helper likewise waits
    # minutes before trusting the pool again.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Url,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$UserName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Password,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$NewMasterUuid,
        [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 600,
        [int]$IntervalSeconds = 5
    )
    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
    $lastError = $null
    while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
        try {
            $session = Connect-Example -Url $Url -UserName $UserName -Password $Password
            $master = (Get-XenPool | Select-Object -First 1).master
            # The new coordinator answers before the pool has settled - calls made too soon fail
            # (HANDLE_INVALID on the operation's own task) - so also wait for every host to be back,
            # live and enabled.
            $settled = (Get-XenHost -Ref $master.opaque_ref).uuid -eq $NewMasterUuid -and
                -not (Get-XenHost | Where-Object {
                    -not $_.enabled -or -not (Get-XenHostMetrics -Ref $_.metrics.opaque_ref).live
                })
            if ($settled) { return $session }
            $session | Disconnect-XenServer
            $lastError = "the pool has not settled under the new coordinator"
        }
        catch { $lastError = $_ }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds $IntervalSeconds
    }
    throw "the pool did not come back after the master change: $lastError"
}

function Enable-WhenBooted {
    # Re-enable a host that has just come back. It reports itself live before xapi on it has finished
    # starting, and until then Enable fails HOST_STILL_BOOTING - so retry that.
    param($XenHost, [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 600, [int]$IntervalSeconds = 10)
    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
    while ($true) {
        try { $XenHost | Invoke-XenHost -XenAction Enable; return }
        catch {
            $ex = $_.Exception
            while ($ex -and -not $ex.ErrorDescription) { $ex = $ex.InnerException }
            if (-not ($ex -and $ex.ErrorDescription -and $ex.ErrorDescription[0] -eq "HOST_STILL_BOOTING") `
                    -or (Get-Date) -gt $deadline) {
                throw
            }
            Start-Sleep -Seconds $IntervalSeconds
        }
    }
}

function Wait-ForRestart {
    # Wait for a host to come back from a reboot (Key "boot_time") or toolstack restart
    # ("agent_start_time"): until that other_config entry differs from -Before and the host is live.
    # Reconnects every time round, because the host restarting may be the coordinator this session
    # talks to; returns the new session.
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Url,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$UserName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Password,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$HostUuid,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Key,
        $Before,
        [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 1800,
        [int]$IntervalSeconds = 10
    )
    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
    while ($true) {
        try {
            $session = Connect-Example -Url $Url -UserName $UserName -Password $Password
            $xenHost = Get-XenHost -Uuid $HostUuid
            if ($xenHost.other_config[$Key] -ne $Before -and (Get-HostLive $xenHost)) { return $session }
            $session | Disconnect-XenServer
        }
        catch {
            # down, or xapi still starting: a connection error or any XenAPI failure, keep retrying.
        }
        if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) { throw "host $HostUuid did not come back in time" }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds $IntervalSeconds
    }
}
```

## xe CLI

```bash
# The one place the connection details live: every example just calls `xe <command> ...`.
xe() {
    # xe reports a failure on stdout. Captured by $(...), that text would land in the variable and set -e
    # would then stop the script without saying why, so pass a failure's output on to stderr instead.
    local out rc=0
    out=$("${XE_EXE:-xe}" -s "$host" "${xe_opts[@]}" -u "$user" -pw "$pass" "$@") || rc=$?
    if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then [ -z "$out" ] || printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return $rc; fi
    [ -z "$out" ] || printf '%s\n' "$out"
}

# A pool member refuses every command with HOST_IS_SLAVE, naming the coordinator's address; send
# everything there instead (assuming the coordinator is up), as XenCenter does when you add a member server.
_probe=$(xe pool-list --minimal 2>&1) || true
if [[ $_probe =~ (Master|Coordinator)\ IP\ address:\ ([0-9A-Fa-f.:]+) ]]; then host=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}; fi

# Bash helpers for `--minimal` (comma-separated) output, so no cut/tr/wc/grep processes are spawned:
first_csv()  { echo "${1%%,*}"; }                       # first element of a comma-separated list
count_csv()  { local IFS=,; set -- $1; echo $#; }       # number of elements (0 for empty)
each_csv()   { local IFS=,; set -- $1; printf '%s\n' "$@"; }   # one element per line, for `for`
nth_csv()    { local n=$2 IFS=,; set -- $1; shift $((n - 1)); echo "$1"; }  # Nth element, 1-based
# A set-valued FIELD (vm-param-get param-name=VBDs, allowed-VBD-devices, ...) is printed "a; b; c" - with
# or without --minimal, which only turns a LIST of objects into a comma-separated line. Convert it, so the
# helpers above work on both.
set_to_csv() { echo "${1//; /,}"; }

shared_sr() { first_csv "$(xe sr-list name-label="Shared NFS" --minimal)"; }
first_host() { first_csv "$(xe host-list --minimal)"; }
vm_uuid()  { first_csv "$(xe vm-list name-label="$1" --minimal)"; }

# Detach an SR from every host, then forget it: XenCenter's Detach followed by Forget. sr-forget refuses an
# SR that is still attached (SR_HAS_PBD), so unplug its PBDs first. Forgetting drops the pool's record of the
# SR but leaves the data on the storage itself.
detach_and_forget_sr() {
    local pbd
    for pbd in $(each_csv "$(xe pbd-list sr-uuid=$1 currently-attached=true --minimal)"); do
        xe pbd-unplug uuid=$pbd
    done
    xe sr-forget uuid=$1
}

# The text content of the first <tag>...</tag> in an XML fragment, using parameter expansion only (no
# xmllint, and no sed/grep process per tag).
xml_tag_text() {
    local xml=$1 tag=$2 rest
    rest=${xml#*<$tag>}
    [ "$rest" != "$xml" ] || return 1
    echo "${rest%%</$tag>*}"
}

# Pick the IQN from an iSCSI discovery probe's XML: the caller's, if named (it must be one the target
# offers), else the first. An array usually offers many targets - one per LUN, often belonging to different
# users - so on shared storage always name yours: sr-create formats the LUN behind it.
choose_target_iqn() {
    local rest=$1 target=$2 wanted=$3 first="" iqn
    while [[ $rest == *"<TargetIQN>"* ]]; do
        rest=${rest#*<TargetIQN>}; iqn=${rest%%</TargetIQN>*}
        [ -n "$first" ] || first=$iqn
        if [ -n "$wanted" ] && [ "$iqn" = "$wanted" ]; then echo "$iqn"; return 0; fi
    done
    if [ -n "$wanted" ]; then echo "target $target does not offer IQN $wanted" >&2; return 1; fi
    echo "$first"
}

# Return the XML a backend sends back on its deliberately-failing discovery probe (args: sm-type, then
# any sr-probe arguments such as host-uuid=/device-config:key=value). The New SR wizard (and XenRT)
# discover iSCSI/HBA LUNs by asking with an incomplete device-config on purpose: the backend can't create
# anything from it yet, so it fails with an SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_<n> whose error parameters carry an XML
# fragment describing what it found - the IQNs on offer, then the LUNs behind one of them, or - for HBA -
# every LUN visible at all. A probe that unexpectedly succeeds means the device-config was already
# complete - not the discovery prompt this helper is looking for. Never probe by attempting sr-create
# instead: on real storage a create that succeeds formats the LUN.
probe_for_failure() {
    local sm_type=$1 out line xml=""
    shift
    if out=$(xe sr-probe type="$sm_type" "$@" 2>&1); then
        echo "SR.probe for $sm_type succeeded without asking for more information;" \
             "check the target address" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # xe prints a known error as "Error code: ..." then "Error parameters: a, b, ..." (the Windows xe.exe
    # that ships with XenCenter says "Error params:"): the XML fragment is always the last parameter xapi
    # sends back, so it runs from the first '<' on that line to the end of the output (a real host
    # pretty-prints it over many lines).
    local in_params=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [ -n "$in_params" ]; then
            xml+=$'\n'"$line"
        else
            case "$line" in
                "Error param"*":"*"<"*) xml="<${line#*<}"; in_params=1 ;;
            esac
        fi
    done <<< "$out"
    if [ -z "$xml" ]; then
        echo "$out" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    echo "$xml"
}

# A throwaway self-signed certificate and private key (PEM), the way XenRT provisions one for its own
# certificate tests. bash has no native crypto library, so shell out to openssl - the same tool XenRT
# itself uses for this.
self_signed_cert() {
    local certfile=$1 keyfile=$2
    openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout "$keyfile" -out "$certfile" \
        -days 365 -subj /CN=sdk-example 2>/dev/null
}

# Wait out a pool-wide xapi restart (pool-designate-new-master) and find the new coordinator's address,
# updating $host - xe does not follow HOST_IS_SLAVE itself (see the probe at the top of this script).
#
# pool-designate-new-master returns BEFORE the change: for a while the old coordinator still answers, and
# still says it is the coordinator, until xapi restarts across the pool. So reconnecting is not enough -
# keep reconnecting until the pool names the new coordinator (by uuid) AND every host is back, enabled and
# live. XenRT's own helper likewise waits minutes before trusting the pool again.
reconnect_after_master_change() {
    local new_master_uuid=$1 timeout=600 interval=5 probe
    local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout))
    while [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ]; do
        # Called as an if-condition, so set -e does not end the script when one of its xe calls fails -
        # and while xapi restarts across the pool, any of them can.
        if probe=$(xe pool-list --minimal 2>&1) && pool_settled_under "$new_master_uuid" "$probe"; then
            return 0
        fi
        if [[ $probe =~ (Master|Coordinator)\ IP\ address:\ ([0-9A-Fa-f.:]+) ]]; then
            host=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
        fi
        sleep "$interval"
    done
    echo "the pool did not come back after the master change" >&2
    return 1
}

# True once the pool (uuid $2) names $1 as its coordinator AND every host is back, enabled and live. The
# new coordinator answers before the pool has settled - calls made too soon fail (HANDLE_INVALID on the
# operation's own task) - hence the second half.
pool_settled_under() {
    local master h
    master=$(xe pool-param-get uuid="$(first_csv "$2")" param-name=master) || return 1
    [ "$master" = "$1" ] || return 1
    for h in $(each_csv "$(xe host-list --minimal)"); do
        [ "$(xe host-param-get uuid=$h param-name=enabled)" = "true" ] || return 1
        [ "$(host_live "$h")" = "true" ] || return 1
    done
}

# Poll host_metrics.live until it matches, rather than issuing the next power command immediately - real
# out-of-band power control has no retry of its own, so a script that doesn't wait can issue a second
# command while the first is still in flight.
wait_for_host_live() {
    local h=$1 want=$2 timeout=${3:-60} interval=${4:-2}
    local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout))
    while [ "$(host_live "$h")" != "$want" ]; do
        if [ $SECONDS -gt $deadline ]; then
            echo "host did not reach live=$want in time" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        sleep "$interval"
    done
}

# Wait for a host to come back from a reboot (key "boot_time") or toolstack restart
# ("agent_start_time"): until that other-config entry differs from $before and the host is live. Follows
# HOST_IS_SLAVE-style coordinator redirection (updating the global $host, the same way the top-of-script
# probe and reconnect_after_master_change do) in case the host restarting is the coordinator xe is
# currently talking to.
wait_for_restart() {
    local host_uuid=$1 key=$2 before=$3 timeout=${4:-1800} interval=${5:-10} probe
    local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout))
    while true; do
        if probe=$(xe host-param-get uuid=$host_uuid param-name=other-config param-key=$key 2>&1); then
            if [ "$probe" != "$before" ] && [ "$(host_live "$host_uuid")" = "true" ]; then
                return 0
            fi
        elif [[ $probe =~ (Master|Coordinator)\ IP\ address:\ ([0-9A-Fa-f.:]+) ]]; then
            host=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
        fi
        if [ $SECONDS -gt $deadline ]; then
            echo "host $host_uuid did not come back in time" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        sleep "$interval"
    done
}

# Re-enable a host that has just come back. It reports itself live before xapi on it has finished
# starting, and until then host-enable fails HOST_STILL_BOOTING - so retry that.
enable_when_booted() {
    local h=$1 timeout=600 interval=10 err
    local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout))
    while true; do
        if err=$(xe host-enable uuid=$h 2>&1); then return 0; fi
        # xe prints the error's message, not its code: HOST_STILL_BOOTING reads "The host toolstack is
        # still initialising".
        case "$err" in
            *STILL_BOOTING*|*"still initialising"*) ;;
            *) echo "$err" >&2; return 1 ;;
        esac
        if [ $SECONDS -gt $deadline ]; then echo "$err" >&2; return 1; fi
        sleep "$interval"
    done
}

# A throwaway VM with a working guest OS: a copy of an existing VM that has one. Suspend, checkpoint,
# live migration and clean shutdown all need the guest's cooperation: on a running VM with no PV drivers
# xapi refuses them up front with VM_LACKS_FEATURE (a VM freshly installed from a template has no OS at
# all). So copy a VM that does have an OS and PV drivers, without disturbing it: snapshot it (fine while
# it runs), then vm-install from the snapshot - a clone-and-provision in one step, straight onto the same
# SR as the snapshot's own disks (vm-install refuses an explicit sr-uuid/sr-name-label when installing
# from a snapshot). The snapshot is only needed for the install, so it goes again straight away.
copy_of_guest() {
    local source_vm_name=$1 new_vm_name=$2 source snapshot vm
    source=$(vm_uuid "$source_vm_name")
    snapshot=$(xe vm-snapshot uuid=$source new-name-label="${new_vm_name}-source")
    vm=$(xe vm-install template-uuid=$snapshot new-name-label="$new_vm_name")
    # Even with force=true, *-uninstall prints the items it destroys on stdout: keep that out of the
    # value this function returns.
    xe snapshot-uninstall snapshot-uuid=$snapshot force=true >/dev/null
    echo "$vm"
}

# Wait, after vm-start, until the guest's PV drivers have reported in. xapi only offers the
# guest-dependent operations once the guest says it can do them, and allowed-operations is where it says
# so: wait for clean_shutdown to appear there (the same check that refuses it with VM_LACKS_FEATURE
# beforehand). A Linux kernel offers that early in boot, before the agent runs (hot-plug needs the agent,
# and suspend needs its emulated disk unplugged), so wait for PV-drivers-detected too. A booting OS takes a
# while.
wait_for_guest_agent() {
    local vm=$1 timeout=${2:-300} interval=${3:-2}
    local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout))
    while true; do
        case "$(xe vm-param-get uuid=$vm param-name=allowed-operations)" in
            *clean_shutdown*)
                [ "$(xe vm-param-get uuid=$vm param-name=PV-drivers-detected 2>/dev/null)" = true ] && return 0 ;;
        esac
        if [ $SECONDS -gt $deadline ]; then
            echo "the guest's PV drivers did not report in within ${timeout}s; does the source VM have" \
                 "a guest OS with PV drivers (XenServer VM Tools)?" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        sleep "$interval"
    done
}

# Relocate every one of a (not-yet-started) VM's disks onto the given SR, the same vdi-pool-migrate
# storage-migrate already demonstrates.
move_disks_to_sr() {
    local vm=$1 sr_ref=$2 vbd vdi
    for vbd in $(each_csv "$(set_to_csv "$(xe vm-param-get uuid=$vm param-name=VBDs)")"); do
        [ "$(xe vbd-param-get uuid=$vbd param-name=type)" = "Disk" ] || continue
        vdi=$(xe vbd-param-get uuid=$vbd param-name=vdi-uuid)
        if [ "$(xe vdi-param-get uuid=$vdi param-name=sr-uuid)" != "$sr_ref" ]; then
            xe vdi-pool-migrate uuid=$vdi sr-uuid=$sr_ref
        fi
    done
}
```
